faq.a: Sex addiction, also called compulsive sexual behavior, is when sexual thoughts, urges, or behaviors, including porn, feel out of control and keep causing harm, even when you want to stop. The World Health Organization lists compulsive sexual behaviour disorder in its ICD-11. A therapist who works with it can help you figure out what's going on for you.

Betrayal trauma is the shock and pain that can follow finding out a partner has been unfaithful or hiding sexual behavior. Trouble sleeping, racing thoughts, checking for clues, and not trusting your own judgment are all common. These are normal reactions to a real injury, and you deserve support for yourself.

faq.q: Can a relationship survive infidelity or sex addiction?
faq.a: Many couples do rebuild, but it takes time and it isn't guaranteed. It usually takes ongoing honesty from the person who broke trust, support for both partners, and patience with a timeline that belongs to the hurt partner. Whether to stay is the hurt partner's decision to make, in their own time.

A 90-day detox, also called sexual sobriety or abstinence, is a common step in sex addiction recovery. It gives you space to heal, figure out your triggers, and build new ways to cope. The goal is to reset unhealthy patterns and work toward healthy intimacy, not to give up sex forever. Plan it with your therapist, and talk it through with your partner if you're in a relationship.

faq.q: What does "disclosure is better than discovery" mean?
faq.a: Telling the truth yourself, ideally with help from a therapist, does less damage than your partner finding out on their own. When they find out on their own, they're hurt by the behavior and by the hiding.

faq.q: What should I do when an urge hits?
faq.a: Put space between you and the urge. Leave the room, put your phone somewhere else, and call or text someone. Urges come in waves, and they pass if you ride them out. The Help now page has a timer and a breathing guide.

faq.q: Where can I find a support group?
faq.a: Sex Addicts Anonymous (SAA) and Sex and Love Addicts Anonymous (SLAA) hold free 12-step meetings for people in recovery. S-Anon and COSA are for partners and family. Recovering Couples Anonymous is for couples. The Sex Addiction group sessions on BetterHelp are another option, and need a BetterHelp membership.

faq.q: I was hurt by my partner. Is any of this for me?
faq.a: Yes. Betrayal hurts, and your healing matters on its own. Pick "I was hurt" at the top of this page to see resources for you. You can also ask your partner to go to their group, take notes, and share them with you after.
